messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a perf cliff in the paged+interleaved path when using bfloat16 on A100s. Microbench shows ~2.8x drop at seq=2048 batch=8 vs expected.

alex: repro: run `./bench_attn --model=7b --seq=2048 --batch=8 --kv-layout=interleaved --dtype=bfloat16 --attn=paged`

alex: quick paste of numbers from my run:
```
# baseline fused (separate layout, bf16)
throughput_tokens/s: 12500
# paged+interleaved (same hw cfg)
throughput_tokens/s: 4400
power: same, memory occupancy slightly higher
```

tanya: ugh. can you include kernel selector logs? also which driver / cuda / cuDNN?

alex: selector log attached below (trimmed). CUDA 11.8, driver 525.60, runtime build a month old. selector: chose paged-fused-variant-v2 -> fallback to paged-kernel-std at runtime.

sam: the numbers smell like bank conflicts / warp divergence. interleaving can create non-coalesced loads for bf16 when stride not aligned. do we have the per-bank stride?

alex: kv layout: interleaved means [batch, head, seq, dim] packed with stride of 384 bytes between heads, dtype=bfloat16 (2 bytes). for our dim=128 and head_count=32 that gives weird alignment when seq%32 != 0.

perf-bot: CI PERF ALERT: benchmark/attn_paged_bf16 (seq=2048,b=8) regressed 2.6x vs baseline. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/bench/attn/1718199999

gary: quick thought: kernel selector currently scores kernels by op_cost + estimated batch_cost ignoring low-level alignment. We should add an "alignment penalty" when (kv_stride_bytes % 128 != 0) or when head_dim%warp_width != 0. Also prefer fused-attn with separate-kv for bf16 if stride looks off. Fallback policy: if warp_efficiency < 70% on sample run, select alternate kernel.

tanya: can we microbench a matrix of seq x batch x layout and collect nsight counters? i can run on canary cluster. will instrument warp_efficiency, l2_bank_conflicts, shared_mem_stall.

alex: ran a quick grid on canary-1, results (excerpt):
```
seq,batch,layout,throughput_tokens/s
512,16,separate,13200
512,16,interleaved,12850
2048,8,separate,12300
2048,8,interleaved,4300  # BAD
3072,4,separate,9800
3072,4,interleaved,3600  # BAD
```

nsys-bot: nv-nsight sample attached: warp_efficiency = 42% for paged+interleaved at seq=2048,b=8; shared_mem_bank_conflicts high, average memory transaction size downshifted.

sam: that's consistent. bank conflicts in shared mem + unaligned vec loads for bf16 when head_dim % 32 != 0. Two mitigation paths: add padding to align to 32/64 bytes (cost: memory); or change kernel selection to avoid paged-interleaved combos for bf16 at those dims.

gary: implementation plan: 1) add alignment-aware score to kernel selector (cheap). 2) add batch-aware check: if batch*seq falls in the 'danger zone' we bias toward separate-kv fused kernel. 3) add a temporary canary config to force separate layout for bf16 models with head_dim%32 != 0.

tanya: +1. also add telemetry to record when selector flips due to alignment so we can measure incidence. I'll draft patch and run canary smoke.

alex: I'll run extended microbench with padding patch to see memory vs perf tradeoff. will post results here.

alex: quick note: this regression only surfaces under mixed workload (high seq, medium batch). low-seq/large-batch still fine. so batching heuristics need to consider seq distribution, not just mean batch size.

tanya: agreed. action items: (1) gary/tanya add selector scoring change + telemetry PR, (2) alex run padding vs selector comparison and upload nsight captures, (3) sam validate bank-conflict fix options. target: canary in 72h. :rocket: 

alex: sgtm, starting runs now. :thumbsup:
